source_landscape: Standard astronomy reference material (encyclopedic, stable): comets are ice-and-dust bodies that develop a coma and tails near the Sun; asteroids are rocky/metallic bodies, concentrated in the main belt; both are leftovers from Solar System formation.
note: AUDITED 2026-09-06 — re-verified against standard astronomy references (composition: ice-and-dust vs rocky/metallic bodies; coma and tails develop near the Sun; main-belt concentration between Mars and Jupiter; both are leftovers from Solar System formation; comets on more eccentric orbits). Statements are deliberately atomic (one fact each) so ordinary verifier-shaped answers match; compound answers that fuse several facts may under-match and are best stated separately.

expected_claims.statement: Comets consist largely of ice and dust.
Comets are icy bodies made of dust.
expected_claims.variant_of: Comets consist largely of ice and dust.
expected_claims.note: Alternate phrasing of the composition base fact, so natural wording like this credits the same fact without inflating the recall denominator.

expected_claims.statement: Asteroids are rocky or metallic bodies.
Comets develop a coma and tails as they approach the Sun.
Both comets and asteroids are small bodies left over from the formation of the Solar System.
Most asteroids orbit the Sun in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Comets typically travel on more eccentric orbits than main-belt asteroids.
expected_claims.note: Orbital contrast; generally true, with nuance around scattered populations.
